"法拉利已做出自己的选择，对弗雷德·瓦塞尔及其团队的领导层拥有完全的信任，我们将继续如此"；天空体育将从周五上午开始现场直播F1巴林大奖赛，F1重返马来西亚，雪邦赛道承办比赛
在克里斯蒂安·霍纳暗示对该职位感兴趣、外界对其未来的猜测升温之后，法拉利重申对领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔的"完全信任"，这家意大利车企明确表示，在由谁执掌F1车队的问题上"已做出自己的选择"。
瓦塞尔在上周六的阿塞拜疆大奖赛后承认，围绕他在车手界（Scuderia）职位的持续且"令人沮丧"的传闻，让车队"并非在完全平静的氛围中工作"。
上周，《泰晤士报》刊登的对霍纳的采访进一步放大了这一说法。这位前红牛车队领队在采访中表示，法拉利是唯一能让他愿意重返车队指挥墙的队伍，而且即使不获得他此前一直坚持作为回归条件的股权也可以。

在本周末巴林大奖赛之前，法拉利于周二上午在马来西亚临时安排了一场不同寻常的媒体简报会，法拉利一位女发言人明确表示，公司高层对瓦塞尔继续执掌车队F1事务抱有充分信心。
这位发言人说：“法拉利的立场是明确且不会改变的。”
“法拉利已经做出了自己的选择，对弗雷德·瓦塞尔及其团队的领导能力抱有充分信心，我们将继续如此。”
“法拉利一直备受关注，这反映了法拉利所代表的意义。我们今天这么说，是因为我们想避免在马来西亚出现流言和猜测，专注于本周末的比赛。”
这位发言人表示，这是对“不仅是《泰晤士报》上关于霍纳先生的那篇文章，还有此后不断增多而非平息的一系列报道”的回应。
瓦塞尔自2023赛季初从索伯加盟以来，已进入执掌车队的第四个赛季，并于去年签署了多年的续约合同。
当被问及瓦塞尔是否仍获得法拉利董事长约翰·埃尔坎和首席执行官贝内代托·维尼亚的全力支持、并将在合同剩余时间内留任时，发言人重申：“法拉利的立场是明确且不变的。”
“法拉利已经做出了自己的选择，他们信任弗雷德·瓦塞尔，我们会继续如此。”

detailEn: Frederic Vasseur: Ferrari state 'full confidence' in F1 team principal after Christian Horner comments and speculation

"Ferrari has made its choices and has full confidence in the leadership of Fred Vasseur and his team and we will continue to do so"; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia live on Sky Sports from Friday morning F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix

Ferrari have reiterated their "full confidence" in Frederic Vasseur as team principal after speculation around his future was fuelled by Christian Horner suggesting interest in the role, with the Italian marque making clear it "has made its choices" around who leads the F1 team.
Vasseur admitted after last Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix that the team were "not working in perfect serenity" amid persistent and "frustrating" rumours around his position at the Scuderia.

That was amplified last week by an interview with Horner published in The Times in which the former Red Bull team principal said Ferrari were the only outfit he would consider returning to the pit-wall for without the ownership stake that he has been prioritising for any comeback to the sport.

In the unusual step of a hastily arranged media briefing on Tuesday morning ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, a Ferrari spokeswoman made clear the company's senior leadership had full confidence in Vasseur to continue running their F1 operation.
"Ferrari's position is clear and unchanged," said the spokesperson.
"Ferrari has made its choices and has full confidence in the leadership of Fred Vasseur and his team and we will continue to do so.
"Ferrari has always attracted interest, it's a reflection of what Ferrari represents. We say this today because we want to avoid gossip and speculation in Malaysia and focus on the weekend."
The spokesperson said was responding to "not only the piece with Mr Horner in The Times but subsequent stories that have been increasing, not dying down".
Vasseur is in his fourth season in charge since joining from Sauber from the start of the 2023 season and signed a multi-year contract extension last year.

Asked if Vasseur retained the full support of Ferrari chair John Elkann and chief executive Benedetto Vigna and would stay in post for the remainder of his contract, the spokesperson reiterated: "Ferrari's position is clear and unchanged.
"Ferrari has made its choices, it has confidence in Fred Vasseur and we continue to do so."

detailEn: United States GP: Lewis Hamilton fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice ahead of Qualifying in Austin

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton outpaced Red Bull's Max Verstappen in final practice in Austin with Friday's pace-setter Charles Leclerc in third; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday
Lewis Hamilton claims the fastest lap from Max Verstappen in final practice at the United States Grand Prix
Lewis Hamilton topped final practice from Max Verstappen at the United States Grand Prix to set up a tantalising qualifying in Austin.
Hamilton was 0.168s quicker than Verstappen as Ferrari and Red Bull look set to fight for pole position and victory for a second consecutive weekend.
Charles Leclerc topped both of Friday's sessions and had set the quickest time in final practice by one tenth from Hamilton, only for it to be deleted due to track limits.

Track limits is set to be a major issue for the drivers in qualifying, which takes place at 10pm UK time later on Saturday (build-up from 8.30pm live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event) due to the tarmac run-off areas and the drivers keen to use every bit of track to gain lap time.

Leclerc still finished the session in third, ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli whose chances of becoming the youngest world champion look extremely difficult, given he must first win the Grand Prix to give himself an opportunity, and Mercedes are a tad off the pace.
Antonelli was three tenths behind Hamilton's pace-setting time with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in fifth at nearly half a second down.

McLaren's Lando Norris was eighth but would have been in the top five had his best lap not been deleted for track limit, while Oscar Piastri was sixth and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg impressing in seventh.
